correctness.rationale: Binary x-coordinates force extremality of every lifted support. For any representation of the midpoint with a large endpoint S, take S\T nonempty by swapping if needed. Coordinates on S∩T and outside S∪T are fixed. For every missing-side a in S\T, each r-monomial of S containing a is bounded by x_a and has the same mean 1/2, so equality holds almost surely. Including any two such a in one r-set makes all these indicators one Bernoulli variable Z. An (r−1)-subset of S meeting S\T has product Z; adjoining any b in T\S yields a midpoint monomial of mean zero. Therefore x_b vanishes on Z=1 and its mean 1/2 forces x_b=1−Z. The midpoint is supported only on the given endpoints, hence their minimal face is the edge (a relative-interior point of a larger face admits representations using its other vertices). With both endpoints small, setting the sum of monomial coordinates to zero gives a face, projecting to the cube with sum ≤r−1. Its vertices are binary: two fractional coordinates can exchange mass, and a single fractional coordinate can vary unless the integer rank bound is tight, in which case it cannot be fractional. At the midpoint the free-coordinate count is the symmetric-difference size, reduced by exactly one if both endpoints are top-rank. This gives precisely flips and top-rank exchanges. Below top rank there are n flips; at top rank there are r−1 removals and (r−1)(n−r+1) exchanges. Counting flips by direction and lower endpoint gives n times the sum of binomial(n−1,k) for k=0 through r−2, while the exchanges contribute half their incidence count. This verifies the degrees, enumerator, and total edge count. The small simplex graph for r=2 makes the full graph complete; for r≥3 the empty set and a two-set are nonadjacent and have a common large neighbor even at r=n. The inspected finite midpoint-collision script corroborates but cannot replace the all-dimensional argument, since uniqueness among pairs alone does not exclude representations using more vertices.

evidence: Theorem 2 is for the standard relaxation, Theorem 7 characterizes its rank-three Trubin property by absence of bad pairs, and Theorem 8 gives a general upper diameter bound n for the true polytope.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The relaxation is not a broader theorem about the same graph. The rank-three property fails here for n≥4 (e.g. S={1,2,3}, T={4}, with {1,2,4} witnessing the bad pair), and the broad diameter bound does not give the exact graph or exact diameter.

value.rationale: Adjacency is a natural invariant of the true convex hull for a canonical homogeneous monomial lift, especially because relaxation adjacency can differ. The universal clique and rank-face decomposition together decide every edge, degree and sharp diameter for the entire family, rather than merely improving a numerical bound or reproducing the quadratic case. No claim is made about sparse and mixed-degree lifts, pivots, or facets.
